newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 rebounds after Friday downturn.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 rebounds after Friday downturn.

text.p: The Czech PX50 index rose in relatively heavy trading on Monday but dealers said the upturn in some leading shares after sharp losses on Friday may have been overstated.
The PX50 gained 0.66 percent to 518.8 while the RPIX index of continuously traded shares moved up 0.9 percent to 1,070.3.
SPT Telecom, the bourses biggest issue, rose 21 crowns to 3,086 after anouncing a new tarrif structure which would increase prices by a nominal average of four percent with effect from April 1.
Dealers said SPT was trading at 3,085/3,110 per share late on Monday afternoon but predicted a small decline on Tuesday.
"I expect that tomorrow I will see the market between 3,050 and 3,100...perhaps (today) the market a little bit over-reacted," said Petr Koblic of Zivnostenska Banka.
Koblic said trading on Monday again focused on investment funds, especially SPIF Cesky which closed eight crowns higher to 339 in heavy trading.
On the market as a whole, activity was lower than Friday's exceptional levels but remained relatively heavy with turnover of 1.1 billion crowns.
